title: Customer two goes from a provisioned workspace to a served op in any dialect, takes their data out, and no anonymous caller can stream a protected table
intent: BUSINESS_KICKOFF.md section 8 names what stands between today and invoice one. Re-read on 2026-10-11: blocker 4 (idempotent provisioning, 64-bit ids) closed by PV-1; blocker 2's allowlist is gone from the interpreted route (forge-control-plane 6d666cd), but `forge new --dialect` writes the `.forge-interpret` marker only for Rust (forge-cli src/cmd/new.rs:491-493), so a Python, TypeScript or Java workspace pushes and never converges; blocker 3 stands as written: `forge build` is an alias of `wasm-build`, which runs cargo for wasm32-wasip1 (forge-cli src/main.rs:124-128); V-8 has no data export of any kind. The J1-J17 journeys pass (J2 fixed by PS-8 on 2026-09-19), but forge-portal-e2e CI on 2026-10-11 (runs 38118823816, 38115650365) has four reds, two of them auth holes: an anonymous WebSocket subscribe is accepted (multi-protocol.spec.ts:140) and an anonymous SSE subscribe to a non-anon table answers 200 text/event-stream (realtime-sse.spec.ts:72). When every step is done: those reds are green, every dialect's scaffold serves on push, the CLI hands a customer no toolchain, `forge export` writes the caller's data as files, and one spec proves customer two end to end on the dev stack in all four dialects with no operator action between provisioning and a served op. Everything runs against the local dev stack (forge-platform-operations/dev/up-full.sh), not a production deployment (Rory, 2026-10-11). The plan lands each step as it finishes (landing block), the first plan to run on landing-discipline-2026-10.

landing.authorized_by: Rory, 2026-10-11 (start the invoice path plan; land everything, run against the dev stack, not a real deployment)

out_of_scope: A production node: buying a server, DNS, the Cloudflare origin cert, genesis.sh, GCP KMS, R2, and the bootstrap-script fixes a real box needs. Rory, 2026-10-11: this plan runs against the dev stack, not an actual deployment.

forge-portal-web's published docs (content/docs/cli.json, deploying.json) that still teach `forge build`: that repo is not in this plan's landing block; name the pages in IP-3's report so a follow-up can land them.
Moving micro-crm-app (forge-portal-e2e fixture) off the cargo/wasm path, and putting specs behind the public forge-crm.

The three pre-diligence fixes (FORGE_RLS_ADMIN_EXEMPT_WRITE, a real KeyProvider with crypto-shred, CAS ledger row rewrite) and self-serve billing; BUSINESS_KICKOFF section 8 puts them on the raise, not invoice one.
An operator-run export that reads every row: it would be a system-tier read of customer data on a customer path, which BOUNDARIES forbids.

vision.moves: A second customer goes from a provisioned workspace to a served op in any of the four dialects with no toolchain and no operator action, can take their data out as files, and cannot have a protected table streamed to an anonymous caller.
vision.unit: V-2 customer-side toolchains the CLI hands over: 1 today (`forge build` runs cargo for wasm32-wasip1), 0 after. V-8 customer data that exports: none today, every table the caller's identity can read after. V-10 failing specs in forge-portal-e2e CI: 4 today, 0 after, plus one spec proving customer two in all four dialects.
vision.if_none: Rows move (Hosting and deploy, Realtime); the customer-facing claim behind every step is that an engagement can be sold on V-2 and V-8 without an operator in the loop.
vision.forbids_checked: V-2: nothing here builds for the customer, and the one verb that did is retired rather than renamed. V-8: export writes plain JSONL the customer holds under their own identity, and nothing makes leaving harder. V-10: this plan asserts no ledger row in public, and each change lands with the spec that proves it.

steps.title: An anonymous WebSocket or SSE subscribe to a table that does not admit anonymous reads is refused
steps.notes: forge-portal-e2e CI 2026-10-11 (runs 38118823816, 38115650365): multi-protocol.spec.ts:140 (P2.2) finds an anonymous WebSocket subscribe accepted, and realtime-sse.spec.ts:72 finds an anonymous SSE subscribe on a non-anon table answering 200 text/event-stream. Both are reads of a protected table by nobody, and a customer's data must not go into a workspace while they stand. Storage runs under the caller's RLS (CLAUDE.md), so find where the realtime routes skip the auth/RLS context the HTTP data API applies, and refuse at subscribe time with the same status the data API gives an anonymous read of that table. A table that does admit anonymous reads stays subscribable anonymously. Re-read at intake 2026-10-11: no runtime hole. probe_items' select policy `title neq "__never__"` (added by forge-portal-e2e b906f9b, PS-1, 2026-09-19) is a literal predicate, which forge-storage crud_emitter.rs has_public_read_policy treats as publicly readable: get/list/query/subscribe are all AuthLevel::Anonymous, and an anonymous REST list of probe_items answers 200 too. The two specs' premise (probe_items is non-anon) went false with PS-1. probe_locked (no select policy) is the only private probe table. The fix is the specs' target table; forge-runtime gains the missing coverage (no test subscribed anonymously over the WS mux at all) pinning both halves of the contract.
acceptance: forge-runtime tests subscribe anonymously over the WebSocket mux and over SSE to a table with no anonymous read policy and are refused (WebSocket: an error frame, never subscribed or event; SSE: 401 with a Bearer challenge, not text/event-stream).
The same tests show an anonymous subscribe to a table whose select policy is a literal predicate (anon-readable) still streams, over both transports.

forge-portal-e2e multi-protocol.spec.ts P2.2 and realtime-sse.spec.ts 'anon subscribe on a non-anon table is refused' target a table that is in fact private, fail on the dev stack before that change and pass after, with the run's output in the step's evidence.
evidence: forge-runtime f8fa258f (lane step-ip1): tests/realtime_anon_subscribe.rs pins both halves over both transports on notes_locked (no select policy) and notes_public (literal-predicate select). Before the WS mux fix (ip1-before, 2026-10-11 21:46): 'test result: FAILED. 3 passed; 2 failed' — anon_ws_subscribe_to_a_public_table_streams ('the anonymous subscriber receives the written row') and ws_resume_of_a_subscription_this_socket_did_not_open_is_refused.

After (ip1-after2, 21:49, fmt + clippy -D warnings + tests): realtime_anon_subscribe 'ok. 5 passed; 0 failed' (anon_ws_subscribe_to_a_private_table_is_refused: error frame UNAUTHENTICATED; anon_sse_subscribe_to_a_private_table_is_401_with_no_stream: 401 + RFC 6750 Bearer challenge, not text/event-stream; anon_ws/sse_subscribe_to_a_public_table_streams; ws_resume_of_a_subscription_this_socket_did_not_open_is_refused: NOT_FOUND); sse_adapter_auth 'ok. 8 passed'; websocket_adapter 'ok. 15 passed'; websocket_adapter_auth 'ok. 7 passed'.

The runtime defect found on the way: the WS mux poll/resume/close dispatched _platform::subscriptions as the subscriber, so an anon subscriber to an anon-readable table got 'subscribed' then POLL_FAILED (no platform:read). They now drain as SSE's drain_identity(); subscribe and command keep the caller's identity, and resume is confined to ids this socket opened (NOT_FOUND otherwise, no dispatch).

forge-portal-e2e edde8ae (lane step-ip1): P2.2 and the SSE anon-refusal spec target probe_locked (probe_items is anon-readable since PS-1 b906f9b). Dev stack (up-full.sh), run ip1-e2e-ba2 2026-10-11 21:58. BEFORE (main 3917e43): '✘ multi-protocol.spec.ts:140:3 … P2.2 an unauthenticated subscribe is refused' — 'Expected: "error" Received: "subscribed"'; '✘ realtime-sse.spec.ts:72:3 … anon subscribe on a non-anon table is refused' — 'anon subscribe must be refused, not an open stream (status 200, ct text/event-stream)'; '2 failed'. AFTER (lane): '✓ multi-protocol.spec.ts:140:3 … P2.2' , '✓ realtime-sse.spec.ts:76:3 … anon subscribe on a non-anon table is refused', '2 passed (1.0m)'. npm run typecheck clean.
implementer report: .harness/report.json (3 verdicts met; gate bundle pre-done-d0b17a85 on forge-runtime f8fa258f)

Landed by hand 2026-10-12 (operator): forge-runtime main e9ed576f..08d3c3ac (origin/main + lane step-ip1 at ab17752a, excluding wip cd807e9e which carried unrelated ingest.rs work the reopened driver wrote after the step was done); landing tree clippy --workspace --all-targets --features adapters -D warnings clean, realtime_anon_subscribe 5, sse_adapter_auth 8, websocket_adapter 15, websocket_adapter_auth 7 passed. forge-portal-e2e main 3917e43..edde8ae, typecheck clean.

steps.title: A workspace scaffolded in any of the four dialects is served on its first push
steps.notes: The interpreted converge only fires for trees with `.forge-interpret` at the root (forge-control-plane src/git/reconcile/interp.rs:51, 55-64; push.rs:137). `forge new --dialect` writes the marker only for Rust (forge-cli src/cmd/new.rs:491-493), while templates/workspace-dialect/README.md:31 tells every user `git push forge main` will serve; an unmarked Python, TypeScript or Java tree with no forge.lock stops at push.rs:847 ('no committed forge.lock; desired-state not updated'). Smallest fix: write the marker for every dialect in scaffold_dialect_workspace. Also remove interp.rs:14-18's stale claim that the route still runs behind the server-build gate (it is open to every workspace since 6d666cd, PS-2). Widened 2026-10-12: a marked Python scaffold converges interpreted but the runtime refuses the bundle ('app_bundle validation failed'): the dialect scaffold declares no app, the CP omits app_manifest for an app-less tree since R-8 (forge-control-plane a818087), and forge-runtime deploy/ingest.rs validate_app_bundle (:645) and ingest_app_bundle (:87) still require it. R-8 checked the trigger and config readers but not the deploy validator; the fix makes an absent app_manifest mean nothing declared in forge-runtime, not a stub app in the scaffold (R-8 retired the zero-surface apps/api workaround).
acceptance: A forge-cli test runs the dialect scaffold for Python, TypeScript, Java and Rust and asserts each tree carries `.forge-interpret`; it fails before the fix for the three non-Rust dialects.
interp.rs's module doc no longer says the interpreted route runs behind the server-build gate.

On the dev stack, a Python workspace made by `forge new --dialect python` and pushed with `forge push` converges and its op answers through the edge; the scripted repro and its output are in the step's evidence.
evidence: forge-cli 9599539 (lane step-ip2): write_dialect_tree writes .forge-interpret for every dialect, not only Rust. New test every_dialect_scaffold_pushes_the_interpret_marker scaffolds Python, TypeScript, Java and Rust and asserts the marker is a file and in git ls-files. Before (redtest, 2026-10-11): 'Python: no .forge-interpret scaffolded / TypeScript: ... / Java: ...', 'test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed'. After (ip2-cli-ladder2): fmt --check, clippy --tests -D warnings and the full forge-cli tests, exit 0 (169 passed, 1 ignored).

steps.title: The customer CLI hands over no toolchain: `forge build` is gone and the wasm verbs are hidden
steps.notes: forge-cli src/main.rs:124-128 declares `wasm-build` with `alias = "build"`; it shells out to cargo for wasm32-wasip1 (cmd/build.rs:80). D-106 (forge-sdlc-harness DECISIONS.md:4926, follow-up at :4975-4978) names this as not done. The customer loop under D-106 is `forge new --dialect`, `forge check`, `forge test`, `forge push`. Drop the alias; mark WasmBuild, WasmUpload and Ship `hide = true` as Deploy and Static already are; they stay callable because forge dev (cmd/dev.rs:226) and dev/up-full.sh's portal ship use them. Hide or retire the four wasm `forge new` templates (WORKSPACE_TEMPLATES in cmd/new.rs). Reword forge-control-plane src/git/reconcile/push.rs:265-270, which tells a pusher to 'Run `forge build`'. Rewrite forge-cli README.md:39-79 around check/test/push. List every forge-portal-web page that still teaches `forge build` in the report; that repo is out of this plan's landing block.
acceptance: A forge-cli test runs `forge build` and gets an unknown-subcommand error, and asserts `forge --help` lists neither wasm-build, wasm-upload, ship nor build; it fails before the change.
`forge new` offers no wasm template to a customer; a test asserts the listed templates.

steps.title: `forge export` writes every table the caller can read as JSONL with a manifest, under the caller's own identity
steps.notes: V-8 has no data export today; `forge pull` fetches only the config tree (forge-cli src/cmd/pull.rs:16-30). Rory, 2026-10-11: the export promises what the caller's identity can read. It rides existing routes, no server or wire change: table list from GET /api/v1/platform/openapi; rows from GET /api/v1/data/{table}?limit=1000&offset=n (forge-storage crates/forge-registry/src/crud_emitter.rs:356-360, limit cap :245); take `as_of` from the first page and pin every later page to it with scope.as_of (forge-storage src/api/dispatch/crud_dispatch.rs:132-168, 244-300) so the export is one consistent cut; an RLS deny-all arrives as the x-forge-rls header (forge-adapters src/http/handler/dispatch.rs:719). Use the CLI's existing bearer (src/client.rs:8-26); never an fr_a_ or fr_p_ token. Tables with api.access hidden, `_` platform tables and blobs have no route: the manifest names them as not exported rather than implying completeness. GET /api/v1/audit/me/export (forge-runtime crates/forge-adapters/src/http/auth_routes/audit/export.rs) is the precedent for exported_at and shape.
acceptance: `forge export --out <dir>` writes <table>.jsonl for every routed table and a manifest.json carrying as_of, per-table row counts, the config tree's git sha, and per-table notes for RLS-denied, hidden and unrouted tables.
A forge-cli test against a stub server asserts one as_of is pinned across every page of a multi-page table, that rows are written exactly once, and that no platform or admin bearer is sent.
On the dev stack, exporting a seeded workspace yields rows equal to what GET /api/v1/data/{table} returns for the same identity, shown in the step's evidence.
forge-cli README.md documents `forge export` and states plainly that it exports what the caller's identity can read.

steps.title: One spec proves customer two end to end on the dev stack in all four dialects
steps.notes: The invoice path's V-10 proof. Against dev/up-full.sh: provision a fresh workspace through the control plane (forge-cp provision; the id is control-plane minted, never supplied), then for each of Python, TypeScript, Java and Rust: `forge new --dialect`, `forge push`, wait for converge, call the op through the edge, write a row, and `forge export` it back. Between provisioning and a served op there is no operator action: no allowlist edit, no env change, no restart. Any dev-stack glue the spec needs (a provisioning helper, a fixture) lands in forge-platform-operations. The spec joins the suite e2e.yml already runs.
acceptance: A forge-portal-e2e spec provisions a fresh workspace and, for each of the four dialects, scaffolds, pushes, gets a served op answer through the edge, writes a row and finds it in `forge export`'s output.
The spec performs no operator action between provisioning and the first served op, and asserts the workspace id came back from the control plane.
The spec passes on the dev stack, with the run's output in the step's evidence, and is part of the suite e2e.yml runs.
